gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you finished the report?' the boss asked. The boss asked ___ finished the report.
gaps.hint: present perfect → past perfect in a yes/no question
gaps.explanation: Have you finished → whether/if I had finished; statement word order throughout.

gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you know the way?' she asked me. She asked me ___ the way.
gaps.explanation: Do you know → if I knew: no do-support in the reported clause.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget your tickets,' she said to us. She ___ us to take our tickets.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' maps onto remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm meeting them tomorrow evening,' she said. She said she was meeting them ___ evening.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow evening becomes the next (or the following) evening.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.
